Pindar, Victory Odes, translated by Arthur S. Way.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/pindar/victory-odes/arthur-s-way

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Pindar, the author, died 450 BC (the facts also list 437 BC; both are ancient) (Wikidata Q134929; Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pindar).
- Arthur S. Way, the translator, died 1930 (Wikidata Q4800630; Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Way).

First publication of the text used: 1922, the translation by Arthur S. Way (SE colophon: 'Victory Odes was completed circa 444 BC by Pindar. It was translated from ancient Greek in 1922 by Arthur S. Way.').

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in 1922, before 1931. Works published before 1931 are in the United States public domain.
- Country of origin: the facts do not name one country of first publication. The possible countries are the United Kingdom, Ireland, the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, India and South Africa. Each of them has a term of life + 70 years or less for these deaths. The last person to die, Arthur S. Way, died in 1930, so the text enters the public domain in each of these countries on 1 January 2001. An unknown exact country, or simultaneous publication in two of them, changes nothing. The original ancient Greek work is public domain in every country, since Pindar died in 450 BC or 437 BC.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."

Sources of these facts:
- SE colophon: Victory Odes was completed circa 444 BC by Pindar. It was translated from ancient Greek in 1922 by Arthur S. Way.
- Pindar: died 450 BC (the facts also list 437 BC; both are ancient).
- Arthur S. Way: death year 1930 from the gathered facts (Wikidata Q4800630; Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Way).
